There are reports that since version 6.7 update-grub fails to find the
device of the root on systems without initrd and on a single device.
This looks like the device name changed in the output of
/proc/self/mountinfo:
6.5-rc5 working
6.7 not working:
and ""update-grub"" shows this error:
/usr/sbin/grub-probe: error: cannot find a device for / (is /dev mounted?)
This looks like it's related to the device name
recognizes the ""/dev/root"" path and tries to find the underlying device.
However there's a special case for some filesystems
particular.
The generic root device detection heuristic is not done and it all
relies on reading the device infos by a btrfs specific ioctl. This ioctl
returns the device name as it was saved at the time of device scan (in
this case it's /dev/root).
The change in 6.7 for temp_fsid to allow several single device
filesystem to exist with the same fsid (and transparently generate a new
UUID at mount time) was to skip caching/registering such devices.
This also skipped mounted device. One step of scanning is to check if
the device name hasn't changed
column2: and if yes then update the cached value.

column1: This broke the grub-probe as it always read the device /dev/root and
couldn't find it in the system. A temporary workaround is to create a
symlink but this does not survive reboot.
The right fix is to allow updating the device path of a mounted
filesystem even if this is a single device one.
In the fix
column2: check if the device's major:minor number matches with the

column1: cached device. If they do
column2: then we can allow the scan to happen so that

column1: device_list_add() can take care of updating the device path. The file
descriptor remains unchanged.
This does not affect the temp_fsid feature
filesystem remains the same and the matching is based on device major:minor
which is unique per mounted filesystem.
This covers the path when the device (that exists for all mounted
devices) name changes
device with filesystem and is not mounted is still skipped.
Note that if a system is booted and initial mount is done on the
/dev/root device
column2: this will be the cached name of the device. Only after

column1: the command ""btrfs device scan"" it will change as it triggers the
rename.
The fix was verified by users whose systems were affected.
